newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures slip on lower LME, dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures slip on lower LME, dollar.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures ended lower on Thursday, hit by a double punch from price declines in London overnight and the dollar's retreat against the yen, traders said.
TOCOM aluminium futures ended 0.9 yen to 1.4 yen lower, with the benchmark February 1998 contract losing 0.9 yen to 204.3 yen per kg.

Traders said TOCOM closely tracked movements in the dollar, which slipped toward 125 yen from well above 126 yen on Wednesday, and prices on the London Metal Exchange overnight, where aluminium shed eight dollars to $1,547 per tonne.
The day's volume was 4,187 lots, well above Wednesday's 3,460 lots and a low of 2,517 on Monday.
"The metal's price could fall below $1,500 in London," said one trader. "It should rebound in the medium term, however. We have seen a constant decline in (LME) stocks."
